title: Distribution-signer / verifier service
goal: Stand up the owner-held, non-worker signing service that independently approves and verifies each cycle's payout manifest before authorizePayout can be produced.
steps: Implement a CLI/service, separate from the scheduler process, with two invocation modes: distribution-signer (reads the compiled manifest + finalized return amount, independently recomputes the root hash/root sum, signs an approval) and verifier (repeats the recomputation from the same finalized snapshot with a second independent key, signs a matching receipt)
Enforce that both signatures reference the exact same rootHash/rootSum before either is considered valid
Add an explicit test asserting the service never reads or holds the scheduler's policy-wallet key material (structural separation, not just convention)
Wire the output into a schema the vault authorizer's PayoutAuthorization step (WP-07) can consume
acceptance: A payout manifest is only usable in a PayoutAuthorization once both the distribution-signer and verifier signatures are present and agree on the same rootHash/rootSum
The service process never has access to the policy-wallet or vault-authorizer key material
A mismatched verifier reconstruction is rejected, not silently accepted
notes: This is the graft from product-first's custody idea (decision D7) closing the tournament's sharpest identified gap: no single compromised worker host can both compute and self-approve a fraudulent manifest. R3, controls payout authorization: per AGENTS.md, use a fresh-context independent reviewer before merge.
